## Page: About Tokeness

URL: https://docs.tokeness.io/about

Tokeness is an AI API gateway for developers. You use one API key and a unified endpoint to call different AI models, then review balance, logs, and usage in the console.

Core facts:

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Product type | AI API gateway |
| Standard Base URL | https://n.tokeness.io/v1 |
| Common protocols | OpenAI Compatible, OpenAI Responses API, Anthropic API |
| Console | https://tokeness.io |
| Documentation | https://docs.tokeness.io |
| Billing model | Prepaid, deducted by actual usage |

Tokeness brings model access, key management, quota control, and usage tracking together in one console. For developers, integration typically only requires configuring the Base URL, API key, and model name; business code continues to call the OpenAI-compatible API as usual.

Common use cases:
- Accessing multiple model providers with a single API key.
- Creating separate API keys for development, production, and customer projects.
- Reviewing call logs, balance, and consumption in the console.
- Letting tools that support a custom OpenAI Base URL connect to Tokeness.

Integration facts:

| Question | Official answer |
| --- | --- |
| What is the OpenAI-compatible endpoint? | https://n.tokeness.io/v1 |
| Where are API keys created? | Tokeness console, API Keys page |
| Where are model names copied from? | Tokeness console or model marketplace |
| Where are prices authoritative? | Console model marketplace or formal quotation |
| Where are call records visible? | Usage logs and dashboard in the console |

Tokeness provides integration guides for OpenAI Compatible API, OpenAI Responses API, Anthropic API, Custom API and Key, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Dify, n8n, Open WebUI and more.

The billing model is prepaid. Each API call is deducted by actual consumption; specific model prices are authoritative in the console. Cost-control tips: use a separate key for each project, set a small quota for development and testing, validate high-consumption tasks with a small sample first, and review usage logs and the dashboard regularly.

Official links:

| Entry | URL |
| --- | --- |
| Website and console | https://tokeness.io |
| Documentation | https://docs.tokeness.io |
| API Base URL | https://n.tokeness.io/v1 |
| Contact | contact@tokeness.io |

## Page: Getting Started

URL: https://docs.tokeness.io/guide/getting-started

Minimum onboarding flow: sign in, top up, create an API key, copy a model name, and make a test request.

Prerequisites:
| Item | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Tokeness account | Registered and signed in to tokeness.io |
| Balance | Top up a small test balance first |
| Model name | Copy one available model name from the model marketplace |
| Test method | Pick one: client, Node.js, Python, or cURL |

Standard configuration:

```txt
Base URL: https://n.tokeness.io/v1
API Key: your Tokeness API key
Model ID: model name copied from the Tokeness model marketplace
```

Key management guidance: use separate keys per project — development/testing keys with small quotas, production keys with clear scope, and one key per customer project for consumption tracking.

Node.js minimal example (create test-tokeness.mjs, replace YOUR_TOKENESS_API_KEY and YOUR_MODEL_NAME):

```ts
import OpenAI from 'openai'

const client = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: 'YOUR_TOKENESS_API_KEY',
  baseURL: 'https://n.tokeness.io/v1'
})

const response = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'YOUR_MODEL_NAME',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Introduce Tokeness in one sentence.' }]
})

console.log(response.choices[0]?.message?.content)
```

Run: npm install openai && node test-tokeness.mjs

If a call fails, check four things first: whether the key was copied completely, whether the account balance is sufficient, whether the model name matches the model marketplace, and whether the Base URL is https://n.tokeness.io/v1.

## Page: OpenAI-Compatible Integration

URL: https://docs.tokeness.io/integrations/openai-compatible

Tokeness exposes an OpenAI-compatible API. Most SDKs, chat clients, and automation tools that support a custom OpenAI Base URL can connect to Tokeness.

Basic configuration:
Base URL: https://n.tokeness.io/v1
API Key: your Tokeness API key

Install the SDK: npm install openai or pip install openai

Node.js example (create test-tokeness.mjs):

```ts
import OpenAI from 'openai'

const client = new OpenAI({
  apiKey: 'YOUR_TOKENESS_API_KEY',
  baseURL: 'https://n.tokeness.io/v1'
})

const completion = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'YOUR_MODEL_NAME',
  messages: [
    { role: 'system', content: 'You are a concise assistant.' },
    { role: 'user', content: 'Say hello from Tokeness.' }
  ]
})

console.log(completion.choices[0]?.message?.content)
```

Python example (create test_tokeness.py):

```py
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="YOUR_TOKENESS_API_KEY",
    base_url="https://n.tokeness.io/v1",
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="YOUR_MODEL_NAME",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello from Tokeness."}],
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

cURL example:

```bash
curl https://n.tokeness.io/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKENESS_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "YOUR_MODEL_NAME", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello from Tokeness."}]}'
```

Model names come from the model marketplace in the Tokeness console. When copying a model name, keep the exact casing, hyphens, and version number.

Common errors:

| Symptom | Possible cause |
| --- | --- |
| 401 or auth failure | Wrong key, key disabled, or Bearer missing from the request header |
| Insufficient balance | Wallet balance too low or key quota exhausted |
| Model does not exist | Model name misspelled, or the model is not available in the current group |
| Bad request format | Non-OpenAI-compatible format used, or Base URL is missing /v1 |

## Page: FAQ

URL: https://docs.tokeness.io/faq

Q: What is Tokeness?
A: Tokeness is an AI API gateway. You use one API Key to call different models and review balance, logs, and usage in the console.

Q: What Base URL should be used?
A: OpenAI-compatible integrations should use https://n.tokeness.io/v1. Do not remove /v1 unless a specific tool explicitly appends it automatically.

Q: Why does authentication fail?
A: Common causes include incomplete API Key copy, missing Bearer header, disabled key, or environment variables not taking effect.

Q: Why does a request show insufficient balance?
A: Tokeness is pre-paid. Check wallet balance and the quota limit configured on the current API Key.

Q: Where should model names be copied from?
A: Copy exact model names from the Tokeness console or model marketplace. Preserve case, hyphens, and version numbers.

Q: Can one key be shared?
A: Technically yes, but separate keys are recommended for development, production, customer projects, and automation tasks.

Q: What tools are supported?
A: Tools that support custom OpenAI Base URL, OpenAI Compatible, Custom Provider, or Custom API can usually connect. Tokeness docs include guides for Claude Code, VS Code + Claude Code, Cline, Roo Code, Continue, Cursor, Codex CLI, Dify, n8n, Open WebUI, AnythingLLM, LibreChat, LiteLLM, OpenClaw, OpenCode, Cherry Studio, and more.

Q: What if the Claude Code command is not found after installation?
A: First confirm Node.js and npm are installed, then restart the terminal. On Windows, use PowerShell, WSL2, or the shell environment recommended by the tool.

Q: What to do when connecting AI coding tools returns 401?
A: Check the API key, Base URL, model name, and protocol type in the tool configuration. For OpenAI-compatible integration, use https://n.tokeness.io/v1 and the header Authorization: Bearer <API Key>.

Q: What is YOUR_MODEL_NAME in examples?
A: It is not a fixed model. Replace it with a real model name copied from the Tokeness model marketplace.

Q: What models does Tokeness support?
A: Tokeness supports multiple mainstream models. The authoritative list is the Tokeness console or model marketplace.

Q: How is Tokeness different from direct OpenAI calls?
A: Tokeness is an OpenAI-compatible gateway. Integrations usually only replace base_url and api_key while retaining OpenAI-compatible request formats. Tokeness adds centralized key management, quota control, usage logs, and multi-model access.

Q: How can Claude Code use Tokeness?
A: Claude Code natively uses Anthropic protocol. Tokeness common access is OpenAI compatible, so use CC Switch to add Tokeness as an OpenAI-compatible provider and enable routing/conversion. Base URL: https://n.tokeness.io/v1.

Q: What payment methods are supported?
A: Current payment methods are shown in the Tokeness console wallet page.

## Page: Models and Billing

URL: https://docs.tokeness.io/billing/pricing

Tokeness uses a prepaid billing model. Each API call is deducted based on actual consumption. Current model prices are authoritative in the console, model marketplace, or formal quotation.

Billing facts:

| Item | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Payment method | Prepaid — top up before calling |
| Deduction method | API call consumption is deducted from the account balance in real time |
| Balance validity | Balance remains valid long-term; specifics are subject to platform policy |
| Price unit | Input and output prices are shown per 1M tokens |
| Exchange rate assumption | Current channel price tables are converted at 1 USD = 7 CNY |

Channel examples: Official-relay channel at API list price or zero markup, Discount channel for some models such as Claude and GPT, Domestic models at Tokeness channel price, Partner discounts available after meeting monthly volume thresholds.

Important: Model supplier prices, exchange rates, and channel policies may change. Public documentation describes the billing method but does not commit to fixed prices.

View consumption in the console: Overview (account and call summary), Data dashboard (model call and consumption trends), Usage logs (individual request status/cost), Wallet (balance and top-up).

Cost control:
1. Use a separate API key for each project.
2. Set a smaller quota for development and test environments.
3. Run high-consumption workflows with a small sample first.
4. Review usage logs and the data dashboard regularly.
5. Split keys by client for channel or client projects.

## Page: Impact Program

URL: https://docs.tokeness.io/partners/impact

Tokeness runs an impact program for open-source projects, public-interest projects, and social enterprises. Selected projects receive 10 million to 5 billion tokens of AI API support per month for development, operations, knowledge services, content production, automated processing, and public service scenarios.

Eligible projects: open-source projects (developer tools, infrastructure, educational resources, accessibility, AI safety), public-interest projects (education, healthcare, environment, disaster response, mental health, rural services, vulnerable group support), and social enterprises (inclusive education, employment for people with disabilities, sustainable consumption, community services).

Monthly quota tiers:
| Tier | Monthly quota | Suitable for |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Starter | 10M tokens | Early-stage projects with public homepage/repo |
| Builder | 50M tokens | Projects with real users or community |
| Growth | 100M tokens | Projects with stable use cases and measurable impact |
| Impact | 500M tokens | Large-scale projects with mature operations |
| Strategic | 5B tokens | High-impact infrastructure or joint projects |

The Strategic tier requires separate review with batched quota release.

Pre-application requirement: Add a Tokeness support statement in a designated public location (repository README.md, website homepage footer, or project release page bottom). Provide HTML/MD code snippets for the attribution link.

Review criteria: Public value and social impact (30%), Project authenticity and operational sustainability (25%), Clarity of AI use cases (20%), Reasonableness of quota needs (15%), Openness and transparency (10%).

Prohibited: selling or gifting impact quota or keys, using impact keys for commercial distribution, illegal activities, malicious consumption, embedding keys in frontend code or public repositories.

Application process: 1) Add support statement. 2) Prepare project intro, public links, use cases, token demand. 3) Email contact@tokeness.io with subject "Impact Program Application - Project Name". 4) Tokeness reviews. 5) Register/confirm Tokeness account. 6) Tokeness issues impact key with quota config. 7) Submit monthly usage report.

Renewal: Monthly review by default. Projects must maintain the public acknowledgment link and submit monthly feedback covering usage, impact results, and next month's plan.

Applications and cooperation inquiries: contact@tokeness.io | Service portal: https://tokeness.io
